ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a game of dominoes the tiles always have to be placed so that the touching halves of two adjacent domino tiles show the same number of dots. Paul has six domino tiles in front of him (see diagram).
<image1>
In several steps Paul tries to arrange them in a correct order. In each step he is either allowed to swap any two domino tiles or he is allowed to turn one domino tile $180^{\circ}$ around. What is the minimum number of steps he needs in order to arrange the domino tiles correctly?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, from left to right there are six dominoes, whose numbers are respectively read as T1=(4|6), T2=(3|1), T3=(4|2), T4=(3|4), T5=(6|1), T6=(2|6). Reasoning: Treat each tile as an undirected edge connecting two numbers. The six edges are 4-6, 3-1, 4-2, 3-4, 6-1, 2-6. Among the degrees of each point, 4 and 6 are odd-degree points, so any correct arrangement must be an Euler trail from 4 to 6 or from 6 to 4. Enumerating Euler trails from 4 to 6, one of them is 4-6-1-3-4-2-6, corresponding to tile order T1,T5,T2,T4,T3,T6. Relative to the initial tile order T1,T2,T3,T4,T5,T6, to obtain T1,T5,T2,T4,T3,T6, at least 2 arbitrary tile swaps are needed; for example, first swap T2 and T5, then swap the tile at current position 3 and T2. In terms of direction, only T2 was originally 3|1, but in the arrangement it needs to be 1|3, so T2 still needs to be flipped once. The total number of steps is 2+1=3. Checking the number of tile swaps plus flips for all Euler trails, there is no case less than 3. Therefore the minimum number of steps is 3.

raw_record.question_text: In a game of dominoes the tiles always have to be placed so that the touching halves of two adjacent domino tiles show the same number of dots. Paul has six domino tiles in front of him (see diagram). In several steps Paul tries to arrange them in a correct order. In each step he is either allowed to swap any two domino tiles or he is allowed to turn one domino tile 180^{\circ} around. What is the minimum number of steps he needs in order to arrange the domino tiles correctly?

method.method_draft: Read the six dominoes from the image, left to right, as T1=(4|6), T2=(3|1), T3=(4|2), T4=(3|4), T5=(6|1), T6=(2|6). Treat each tile as an undirected edge between its two pip numbers. A correct domino row is then an Euler trail using all six edges, with the direction of traversal determining whether a tile must be flipped. The graph has odd-degree endpoints 4 and 6, so every valid row must be a trail from 4 to 6 or from 6 to 4. Enumerate the possible trails and, for each, compute cost = minimum number of arbitrary tile swaps needed to put the tile labels in that order plus the number of tiles whose displayed orientation must be reversed. One cheapest trail is 4-6-1-3-4-2-6, corresponding to tile order T1,T5,T2,T4,T3,T6, with only T2 flipped. This order is obtained from the initial order T1,T2,T3,T4,T5,T6 by two swaps, for example swap T2 with T5, then swap the now-position-3 tile with T2, and then flip T2 to make it 1|3. The final row is 4|6, 6|1, 1|3, 3|4, 4|2, 2|6. The enumeration of all Euler trails shows no trail has swap-cost plus flip-cost below 3, so the minimum is 3.

Paul has six domino tiles in front of him (see diagram). In several steps Paul tries to arrange them in a correct order. In each step he is either allowed to swap any two domino tiles or he is allowed to turn one domino tile 180^{\circ} around. What is the minimum number of steps he needs in order to arrange the domino tiles correctly?

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, from left to right there are six dominoes, whose numbers are respectively read as T1=(4|6), T2=(3|1), T3=(4|2), T4=(3|4), T5=(6|1), T6=(2|6).

Reasoning: Treat each tile as an undirected edge connecting two numbers. The six edges are 4-6, 3-1, 4-2, 3-4, 6-1, 2-6. Among the degrees of each point, 4 and 6 are odd-degree points, so any correct arrangement must be an Euler trail from 4 to 6 or from 6 to 4.

Enumerating Euler trails from 4 to 6, one of them is 4-6-1-3-4-2-6, corresponding to tile order T1,T5,T2,T4,T3,T6. Relative to the initial tile order T1,T2,T3,T4,T5,T6, to obtain T1,T5,T2,T4,T3,T6, at least 2 arbitrary tile swaps are needed; for example, first swap T2 and T5, then swap the tile at current position 3 and T2. In terms of direction, only T2 was originally 3|1, but in the arrangement it needs to be 1|3, so T2 still needs to be flipped once. The total number of steps is 2+1=3.

Checking the number of tile swaps plus flips for all Euler trails, there is no case less than 3. Therefore the minimum number of steps is 3.
